rationale: Gate passes. (1) Reusable: the design document explains why MemKernel's memory tiers work the way they do. It covers the CoALA/Roynard framing, the fast-state/slow-state analogy to HRM, and the JEPA-style dedup proxy. It also maps each mechanism to its source in the literature and to the code that implements it, gives the exact recall and forgetting formulas with per-type half-lives, and states the division of labour between server and agent and the non-goals. Future contributors working on memkernel or the wiki bridge will need all of this. (2) Citable: repo file eval/navigation/corpus/docs/architecture/memory-tiers.md. (3) Non-duplicative: the concept page memkernel-tiered-memory already covers tiers, retention and scoring, and it names this document as its design reference without citing it. The right move is to update that page, not create a new one. The ADR-007 decision page already records the decision and the rejected alternatives, so it is left unchanged. (4) New-contributor-relevant: the mechanism-to-code map and the non-goals are what a newcomer needs to find their way around the code and avoid re-proposing deferred work. Edits: update the concept page and append one log line. No new page is created, so index.md is unchanged.
